FIND: The `HashRing.locate` method in Listing D contains an off-by-one boundary condition bug when a key's hash exactly matches the hash of a virtual node. It uses `bisect.bisect_right`, which returns the insertion point *after* any existing identical entries.
FOLLOW: If a key hashes to the exact same 64-bit integer as a virtual node, it will be routed to the subsequent node on the ring instead of the node that mathematically owns that exact hash. This violates the standard closed-bound expectation `(prev, curr]` of consistent hashing rings, causing boundary keys to be requested from a node that does not expect to own them, potentially causing cache misses or rejected pushes.
ANALYSE: HARD constraint (Mathematical/Algorithmic Correctness). Consistent hashing partitions a ring into intervals owned by nodes. A node at position $P$ owns keys in the range $(P_{prev}, P]$. `bisect_right(keys, H)` returns an index $> i$ if $H == keys[i]$. Thus, the exact boundary $P$ is incorrectly shifted to the next node's interval. CONFIRMED.
FIX: Change `bisect_right` to `bisect_left` so that exact matches return the index of the matching node itself.
